objectives: Recognize bilateral pitting oedema as severe acute malnutrition.
Screen for appetite and medical complications before deciding disposition.
Prioritize urgent referral-level care rather than routine outpatient nutrition advice.
takeaways: Oedema in both feet is a severe malnutrition sign until proven otherwise.
Quiet behavior, poor appetite, and recurrent illness increase complication risk.
HC III should stabilize and refer when severe acute malnutrition criteria are met.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A 3-year-old with swollen feet and poor appetite may have severe acute malnutrition requiring urgent escalation.

sections.title: Caregiver history
sections.text: Swelling started 1 week ago. Child is less playful and has eaten very little for 2 days.

coach.title: Joan appears quiet and thin
coach.body: This is not a vitamins-only visit. First, classify risk using malnutrition danger signs.

sections.title: Nutritional exam
sections.text: Bilateral pitting oedema of both feet and visibly wasted upper arms.

coach.title: What is the most important classification?
coach.body: Choose the diagnosis that changes urgency immediately.

question.prompt: How should bilateral foot oedema be interpreted here?

options.text: Severe acute malnutrition with complications; urgent referral pathway needed
Mild nutrition issue; routine follow-up in one month
Likely simple edema from excess salt intake only
Treat as uncomplicated malaria first because weight is low

question.right: Correct. Bilateral pitting oedema in a child is a severe acute malnutrition sign and requires urgent escalation according to IMNCI/UCG framing.
question.wrong: Both-feet oedema is a red flag for severe acute malnutrition, not a routine finding. Delayed escalation can be dangerous.

sections.title: Disposition
sections.detail: Warmth, hypoglycemia prevention, infection screen, urgent transfer

coach.title: Which next action is safest at HC III?
coach.body: Select the option that addresses severe malnutrition complications.

options.text: Start stabilization steps and arrange urgent referral for severe acute malnutrition care
Send home with appetite stimulant and multivitamins only
Delay referral until child gains weight over two weeks
Treat edema with a diuretic and review later

question.right: Correct. Severe malnutrition with oedema and poor appetite needs urgent higher-level nutrition and medical management.
question.wrong: Outpatient-only approaches are unsafe in oedematous severe malnutrition with poor appetite.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You recognized severe acute malnutrition and escalated care promptly.
sections.emphasis: Bilateral oedema changed the urgency and disposition.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: In child nutrition triage, bilateral pitting oedema is a severe sign. Joan required stabilization and urgent referral rather than routine outpatient advice.
